72:1: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, God has revealed to me that a group of jinn listened to this Qur’an and said to their people when they heard it, Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur’an.
72:2: He guides to the right path. He says: He points to the truth and the right path. So we believed in him. He says: We believed him. And we will not associate anyone with our Lord. Of His creation. The reason why these jinn listened to the Qur’an was as follows: “Muhammad bin Muammar told me, he said: Abu Hisham told us, meaning Al-Makhzumi, he said: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not recite to the jinn nor did he see them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out with a group of his companions, heading for the market of ‘Ukaz. He said: The devils were prevented from receiving report from heaven, and meteors were sent upon them. The devils returned to their people and said: What is the matter with you? They said: We were prevented from receiving report from heaven, and meteors were sent upon us. They said: Nothing prevented you from receiving report from heaven except something that happened. He said: Then go and travel the east and west of the earth and see what happened. He said: So the group set out, traveling the east and west of the earth, seeking to see what prevented them from receiving report from heaven. He said: The group who had headed towards Tihamah set out to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Nakhlah, while he was heading for the market of ‘Ukaz, and he was praying with his companions.” Al-Fajr. He said: When they heard the Qur’an, they listened to it and said: This, by God, is what came between you and the report from heaven. He said: Then when they returned to their people, they said: O our people, Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur’an * It guides to the right path, so we have believed in it, and we will not associate with our Lord anyone. He said: Then God revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “Say, ‘It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened. ’” And what was revealed to him was the words of the jinn. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Warqa’, who said: The group of Zurba’ah and his companions came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca. They heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite, then they left. This is what His statement means: “And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an. And when they attended it, they said, ‘Listen quietly’” (al-Ahqaf 46:46). He said: There were nine of them, including Zurba’ah. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: Regarding His statement, Say, ‘It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened,’ is the statement of God, And when We turned to you a group of the jinn (Al-Ahqaq: 46). The heavens were not guarded during the period between Jesus and Muhammad. When God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the lowest heaven was guarded, and the devils were pelted with meteors. Iblis said, ‘Something has happened on earth.’ So he ordered the jinn to disperse across the earth to bring him report of what had happened. The first to be sent were a group from the people of Nasibin, which is a land in Yemen, and they were the nobles and masters of the jinn. So he sent them to Tihamah and the areas adjacent to Yemen. Those people went and came to the valley of Nakhal, which is two nights’ journey from the valley. They found the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, praying the dawn prayer, and they heard him reciting the Qur’an. When they attended to him, they said, ‘Listen.’ When he finished, meaning he finished the prayer, they returned to their people as warners, meaning Believers whom the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not know about, and he did not feel that it was directed to him, until God revealed to him: Say, ‘It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened.’
72:3: And His saying: And that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is: So we believe in Him and we will not associate anyone with our Lord, and we believe that He, the Most High, commanded us and has authority and power. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord, he said: His action, His command, and His power. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord, meaning: Exalted is the command of our Lord. Muhammad bin Bashar and Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding this verse, Exalted is the Majesty of our Lord, he said: The command of our Lord. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Suddi, Exalted is the majesty of our Lord. He said: The command of our Lord. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Exalted is He! Our Lord has taken neither a wife nor a son, he said: Exalted is He, He commanded him to take, and what they said should not be a wife nor a son. And he recited, “Say, ‘He is God, the One. God, the Self-Sufficient. He neither begets nor is born. And there is none comparable to Him.’” [Surat al-Ikhlas], he said that would not be from Him. Others said: He meant by that the majesty of our Lord and His remembrance. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, who said: Ikrimah said, regarding His statement, The majesty of our Lord, he said: The majesty of our Lord. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Khalid bin Yazid told me, he said: Abu Israel told us, on the authority of Fadil, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And that He, the Most High, is the Majesty of our Lord, he said: The Majesty of our Lord. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, who said: Ikrimah said: Exalted is the majesty of our Lord means the majesty of our Lord. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord: meaning, His majesty, greatness, and command are exalted. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding the Almighty’s statement, Our Lord is in a state of greatness. He said: Exalted is the command of our Lord, exalted is His greatness. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Our Lord is rich. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, who said: Al-Hasan said, regarding the Almighty’s statement, Our Lord is rich, he said: Our Lord is self-sufficient. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of al-Hasan: Exalted is the majesty of our Lord. He said: Our Lord is self-sufficient. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Aliyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, Exalted is the richness of our Lord, he said: Our Lord is self-sufficient. Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of al-Hasan and Ikrimah, regarding the statement of God, And that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord. One of them said: His richness, and the other said: His greatness. Others said: What he meant by that is the grandfather, who is the father of the father. They said: That was from the speech of the ignorant jinn. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abi Sarah told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ja’far, Exalted is the majesty of our Lord. He said: It was the words of the ignorant jinn. Others said: He meant by that: he mentioned it. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Exalted is the majesty of our Lord, he said: He mentioned it. The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our opinion, is the saying of the one who said: What is meant by that is: Exalted is the greatness, power, and authority of our Lord. We said that this is more correct because the grandfather in the speech of the Arabs has two meanings: One of them is the grandfather who is the father of the father, or the father of the mother, and that is not permissible to describe these people whom God described with this description, because they said: So we believe in him and will not associate with our Lord anyone. And whoever describes God as having a son or a grandfather who is the father of the father or the father of the mother, then there is no doubt that he is one of the polytheists. The other meaning is the grandfather that means luck. It is said: So-and-so has luck in this matter, if he has luck in it, and it is what is called in Persian luck. This is the meaning that these people of the jinn intended when they said: And that He, the Most High, is the grandfather of our Lord, God willing. They only meant that his luck in the kingdom, authority, power and greatness is high, so he does not have a companion or a child, because a companion is only for the weak and helpless who is compelled by the desire that motivates him to take her, and a child is only from a desire that drives him to intercourse from which the child occurs. So the people of the jinn said: The kingdom and authority of our Lord are high. His power and greatness are such that He is weak, as are His creation, who are compelled by lust to take a wife or to have intercourse with something from which a child is born. The truth of what we have said about that is demonstrated by God’s statement about them that they declared God free from having a wife or a son, by His statement: And indeed, our Lord, the Most High, has taken neither a wife nor a son. It is said of him: a serious, new, and successful man: meaning he has a share in what he is in. From this is the statement of Hatim al-Ta’i: Attack the Banu Tha'al, for attacking is your grandfather. Run up the hills and do not cry for those who were killed. Another said: Your grandfather raises his voice, I am a man whom the enemies have driven to you in a fit of war. His saying, He has not taken a wife or a son, means a wife. The reciters differed in the reading of His statement, And that He, the Most High, is the One, so Abu Ja`far al-Qari` and six other letters read it with a fat-ha, including (that a group listened, and that the mosques are for God, and that our fool was saying, and that there were men from among mankind, and that when Abdullah stood up to call upon Him, and that if only they were to remain on the path), and Nafi` used to break it except for three letters: one of them is Say, ‘It has been revealed to me that a group listened,’ and the second is And if only they were to remain on the path (al-Jinn 72:16), and the third is And that the mosques are for God (al-Jinn 72:18). As for the reciters of Kufa other than `Asim, they open everything at the end of Surat al-Najm and the beginning of Surat al-Jinn except for His statement, And they said, ‘Indeed, we have heard,’ and His statement, Say, ‘I only call upon my Lord,’ and what follows it to the end of the surah, and they break that except for His statement, That He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord (al-Jinn 72:20). As for `Asim, he used to break all of them except for His statement, And that the mosques are for God (al-Jinn 72:18), for he used to open it. As for Abu `Amr, he He used to break all of them except for His saying, And if they had remained on the right way (al-Jinn 72:16), for he used to open this and what came after it. As for those who opened all of them except in the place of saying, like His saying, And they said, ‘Indeed, we have heard’ (al-Jinn 72:1), and His saying, Say, ‘I only call upon my Lord’ (al-Jinn 72:20), and the like of that, then they connected an in every surah to His saying, So we believed in it, and We believed in all of that, so they opened it by the occurrence of faith upon it. Al-Farra’ used to say: Do not let it prevent you from finding faith ugly in some of that from opening, and that which is ugly with the appearance of faith may be good in it with a present tense verb for faith, so it is necessary to open an as the Arabs said: If the prostitutes appear one day and pluck their eyebrows and blemishes He said: And by saying the accusative, he said: And if only they were to remain on the right path (al-Jinn 72:16), so it is necessary for the one who breaks it to delete an from law because if an is lightened, it is not a narration. Do you not see that you say: I say if you did, I would have done it, and an is not included? As for those who broke it, all of them, while in that they say: And if they were to remain on the right path (al-Jinn 72:16), so it is as if they concealed an oath with law and cut it off from the sequence at the beginning of the speech, so they said: By God, if they were to remain on the right path, he said: And the Arabs include an in this place with the oath and delete it. The poet said: I swear that if anything came to us from his messenger other than you, we would not have found a defense against you. He said: And another recited to us: By God, if you were free, you would not be free, nor would you be a free man. And he included an from the broken particle of all of them, and he put the accusative of and the mosques belong to God (al-Jinn 72:18), because he specified that to the revelation, and he made and if an oath implied in it as I described. As for Nafi’, what he opened of that, he returned it to his saying it was revealed to me and what he broke, he made it from the saying of the jinn, and I like that to read it with the opening in what was revelation, and the breaking in what was from the saying of the jinn, because that is the most eloquent in Arabic, and the clearest in meaning, even though there are other readings whose correctness is not proven.
72:4: God Almighty says, informing us about what was said by a group of jinn who listened to the Qur’an: Our foolish one used to say, meaning Iblis. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And that our foolish one used to say something outrageous about God, meaning Satan. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man from Mecca, on the authority of Mujahid: Our foolish one has transgressed against God, said Iblis. Then Sufyan said: I heard that when a man prostrates, Iblis sits weeping and says: Woe to him, he was commanded to prostrate but he disobeyed, so Hell is his. And the son of Adam was commanded to prostrate and he prostrated, so Paradise is his. Ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Qatada recited: “And that our foolish one used to say an outrage against God. And we thought that mankind and the jinn would never tell a lie about God.” So he said: By God, the foolish one of the jinn disobeyed Him, just as the foolish one of mankind disobeyed Him. As for the extravagance of speech, it is what is transgressive. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And that our foolish one used to say an outrage against God, he said: Unjustly.
72:5: And His statement, And we thought that mankind and the jinn would never tell a lie about God, means: They said: And it is enough for us that the children of Adam and the jinn would never tell a lie about God. And the word thought here means doubt. And these people from the jinn denied that you knew that anyone would dare to lie about God when you heard the Qur'an, because before they heard it and before they knew that those who claimed that God had a wife and a son and other meanings of disbelief denied God, they thought that Iblis was truthful in what he called the children of Adam to of various types of disbelief. So when they heard the Qur'an, they were certain that he was lying in all of that. Therefore, they said, And that our fool was saying something outrageous about God, so they called him a fool.
72:6: And His statement, And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, the Almighty says, informing about what these people said: And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn during their travels when they settled in their homes. This was what they did, as we have been told, like: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, he said: There were men among mankind, one of them would spend the night in a valley during the Age of Ignorance and say: I seek refuge with the Mighty One of this valley, and that increased their sin. Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, he said: When a man among them went down to the valley and spent the night there, he said: I seek refuge with the noble one of this valley from the evil of the foolish ones of his people. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, that when they descended into a valley, they would say, By the master of this valley, from the evil in it. Then the jinn would say, We have no power over you or over ourselves to harm or benefit you. He said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, he said: In the pre-Islamic era, when they descended into a valley, they would say, We seek refuge with the master of this valley, and the jinn would say, You seek refuge with us, and we do not possess any power to harm or benefit ourselves. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They seek refuge in men from among the jinn, he said: They would say when they went down into a valley: We seek refuge in the great ones of this valley. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, it was mentioned to us that when this tribe of Arabs settled in a valley, they would say: We seek refuge with the most honorable people of this place. God said, So they increased them in burden, meaning in sin, and the jinn became more audacious towards them because of that. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They seek refuge with men from among the jinn. In the pre-Islamic era, when they entered a place, they would say: We seek refuge with the most honorable people in this place. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Ar-Rabi` ibn Anas, And that there were men from among mankind who sought refuge with men from among the jinn. He said: They used to say, So-and-so from among the jinn is the lord of this valley. So when one of them entered the valley, he would seek refuge with the lord of the valley instead of God. He said: This would increase his burden, which is the separation. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, but they increased them in burden, he said: In the pre-Islamic era, if a man settled in a valley before Islam, he would say: I seek refuge in the chief of this valley. But when Islam came, they sought refuge with God and left them. And His statement, So they increased their burden, the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is that the people increased their oppression of the jinn by seeking refuge with their noble one, and they increased their sin by that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So they increased their burden means that it increased their sin. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: God said, So they increased their burden, meaning sin, and the jinn became more audacious towards them because of that. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: So they increased their burden meaning: sin. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, So they increased their burden. He said: So they increased their audacity towards them. He said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim, So they increased their burden. He said: They increased their audacity towards them. Others said: Rather, he meant by that that the infidels increased in their transgression. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And they increased them in burden, he said: The disbelievers increased in transgression. Others said: Rather, he meant that, and they increased their fear. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas: So they increased their burden. He said: So that increased their burden, which is separation. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And they increased them in burden, he said: The jinn increased their fear. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of this is: So the people increased the sin of the jinn by doing that, and that is how they increased their permissibility of what God has forbidden. And haraq in the speech of the Arabs means: sin and committing forbidden acts, and from this is the saying of Al-A’sha: Nothing benefits me without seeing her. Will my pain be cured unless it is afflicted with exhaustion? He says: Unless he cheats in a forbidden way.
72:7: God Almighty says, informing us of what these men of the jinn said: And that they thought, as you thought, that God would not send anyone. Meaning that the men of the jinn thought, as the men of mankind thought, that God would not send anyone as a messenger to His creation, calling them to His Oneness. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Al-Kalbi: And they thought as you thought. The unbelieving jinn thought as the unbelieving human beings thought that God would not send a messenger.
72:8: And His statement, And we sought the heaven, God Almighty says, informing us of what these people said: And we sought the heaven and desired it, and found it filled, meaning: We found it filled with strong guards, meaning guardians, and shooting stars, which is the plural of shooting star, and they are the stars with which the devils were stoned. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ziyad, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: The jinn were listening, and when they returned, they said: What happened in heaven is due to something that happened on earth. He said: So they went searching until they saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, coming out of the market of Ukaz, praying the dawn prayer with his companions. So they went to their people as warners.
72:9: God Almighty says: “And indeed, we, the jinn, used to sit in positions in the sky to listen to what was happening and what would be in it. “So whoever listens now” in it from us will find a flaming fire lying in wait for him. Meaning: a flaming fire has been laid in wait for him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We have touched the heaven... to his statement, So whoever listens now will find a flaming fire lying in wait for him. The jinn used to hear the heaven, but when God sent His Prophet, they guarded the heaven and prevented that, so the jinn checked that from themselves. He told us that the nobles of the jinn were in Nasibin, so they asked for that and struck a blow for him until they fell on the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was praying with his companions, heading towards Ukaz. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And we sought the heaven but found it filled with stern guards and meteors… until he reached, So whoever listens now will find a meteor lying in wait for him. When they found that, they returned to Iblis and said: He has prevented us from hearing. So he said to them: The heaven has never been guarded except for one of two matters: Either for a punishment that God wants to bring down suddenly upon the people of the earth, or for a guiding and reforming prophet.
72:10: He said: That is the statement of God: And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth, or whether their Lord intends for them right guidance. God Almighty says, informing about what these people of the jinn said: “And we do not know whether it is a punishment that God intended to bring down on the people of the earth, by preventing us from hearing from the sky and stoning those of us who listened to it with meteors. “Or whether their Lord intended for them right guidance.” He says: Or whether their Lord intended for them guidance by sending from among them a guiding messenger who would guide them to the truth. This interpretation is based on the interpretation that we mentioned from Ibn Zayd before. Al-Kalbi mentioned in this regard: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, on the authority of Al-Kalbi, regarding his statement, And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them right guidance, that they should obey this Messenger so he may guide them or disobey him so he may destroy them. We said the first statement because his saying, And we do not know what evil is intended for those on the earth, follows his saying, And we used to sit there in places to listen... the verse. So it was more appropriate for it to be part of the completion of the story of what preceded it and was close to it, and more appropriate for it to be part of the completion of the report of what came after it.
72:11: God Almighty says, informing us of what they said: And among us are the righteous, meaning the Muslims who work in obedience to God. And among us are those who are less than that, meaning: And among us are those who are less than the righteous. “We were of different ways,” meaning: And we were of different desires and various sects, among us were the believer and the disbeliever. “Ways” is the plural of way, which is the way of a man and his school of thought. Qadd is the plural of Qaddah, which is the different kinds and types. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Hamid Al-Razi told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, different ways, he said: different desires. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “And among us are the righteous, and among us are less than that. We were divided ways.” He said: Various desires, among us are Muslims, and among us are polytheists. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: We were of different ways. The people had different desires. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Different paths he said: Desires. Ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, We were divided into different ways, he said: Muslims and disbelievers. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: We were of different paths. He said: Different, believers and unbelievers. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, We were of different ways, he said, righteous and unbelieving, and he recited the statement of God, And among us are the righteous and among us are less than that.
72:12: And His statement, And we thought that we would never fail God on earth, means: And we knew that we would never fail God on earth if He intended to harm us. And we would never fail Him by escaping, if we sought Him and escaped Him. They only described God as having power over them wherever they were.
72:13: His statement, And when we heard the guidance, we believed in it. He says: They said: And when we heard the Qur’an that guides to the straight path, we believed in it. He says: We believe in it, and we acknowledge that it is the truth from God. So whoever believes in his Lord, will not fear loss or burden. He says: So whoever believes in his Lord will not fear loss: He says: He will not fear that his good deeds will be reduced, so he will not be rewarded for them, nor burden: nor a sin that will be borne by him from the bad deeds of others, or a bad deed that he does. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, He will not fear loss or burden, meaning: He will not fear a decrease in his good deeds, nor an increase in his bad deeds. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, He will not fear loss or burden, meaning: He will not fear that any of his work will be reduced. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He shall not fear loss: meaning injustice, that his good deeds will be wronged and something will be reduced from them, or that the sin of another will be placed on him. Nor burden nor sin. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, So he will not fear any reduction or burden, he said: He will not fear that anything of his reward will be reduced or burdened, so that he will be wronged and not be given anything.
72:14: God Almighty says, informing us about what was said by the group of jinn: And among us are the Muslims who have submitted to God in obedience, and among us are the deviants who are those who have deviated from Islam and the path. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And among us are Muslims and among us are the unjust, he said: Those who deviate from the truth. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, the unjust, he said: the wrongdoers. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: The unjust are the oppressors. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, the unjust, he said: the unjust. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Al-Muqsit is the just one and Al-Qasit is the unjust one, and he mentioned a verse of poetry: Our share of the properties was in the reign of Tubba and before that. I do not know what punishment will come to the souls. He said: This is like the dust and the soil. He said: The dust is the poor person. He read: Or a poor person covered with dust (al-Balad 90:6). He said: The soil is the rich person. And His statement, So whoever submits - those have sought guidance, means: So whoever submits and submits to God in obedience, those have deliberately sought guidance in their religion.
72:15: As for the unjust, the oppressors say about Islam, They were fuel for Hellfire, which is kindled with them.
72:16: God Almighty says: And if these unjust people had been steadfast on the path of truth and righteousness, We would have given them abundant water to drink meaning: We would have provided them with abundant provisions and made things easy for them in this world to test them thereby meaning: to test them thereby. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And if they had remained steadfast upon the way, We would have certainly given them abundant water, meaning by steadfastness: obedience. As for abundant water, it is pure, abundant water. To test them thereby means: To test them with it. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid: And if they had remained steadfast on the way the way of Islam We would have certainly given them abundant water he said: much beneficial, we would have given them much wealth to test them thereby until they return to what was written for them of misery. Ishaq bin Zaid Al-Khattabi told us: Al-Faryabi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ubaid God bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid: And if they had remained steadfast on the way he said: the way of truth We would have certainly given them abundant water he said: a great deal of money to test them thereby he said: to test them with it until they return to the misery that was written for them. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Mujahid, on the authority of his father, the same. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Alqamah bin Marthad, on the authority of Mujahid: And if they had remained steadfast on the way he said: Islam We would have given them abundant water he said: a lot to test them thereby he said: to test them with it. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of more than one person, on the authority of Mujahid: Plentiful water. He said: Water, and plentiful means abundant. That We may test them thereby until they return to My knowledge of them. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, We would have given them abundant water, he said: We would have given them much wealth. His statement, To test them thereby, he said: To test them. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, regarding his statement, And if they had remained on the right way, he said: the religion. We would have given them abundant water, he said: a great deal of money. To test them thereby, he said: to test them with it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And if they had remained steadfast on the way, We would have certainly given them abundant water. He said: If they had all believed, We would have given them plenty of this world. God said, To test them thereby. He said: To test them with it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: We would have given them abundant water to drink. He said: If they had been pious, their provision would have been made abundant. To test them thereby. He said: To test them thereby. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas: Plentiful water means: a comfortable life. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And if they had remained on the right way, We would have certainly given them abundant water, he said: Abundant water means abundant money. To test them with it means to test them with it. Amr bin Abdul Hamid Al-Amili told us: Al-Muttalib bin Ziyad told us, on the authority of Al-Taimi, who said: Omar, may God be pleased with him, said regarding His statement, And if they had remained on the right way, We would have certainly given them abundant water, he said: Wherever there is water, there is wealth, and wherever there is water, there is temptation. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: If they had persisted in misguidance, We would have given them abundant provision to lure them in. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Imran ibn Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, who said: And if they had remained steadfast on the path of misguidance. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: If they had remained steadfast on the path of truth and believed, We would have made things easy for them. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: Concerning His statement, And if they had remained on the right way, he said: This is a parable that God has set forth, like His statement, And if only they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have consumed from above them and from beneath their feet (al-Ma’idah 5:66), and His statement, the Most High, And if only the people of the cities had believed and feared God, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth (al-A’raf 7:36). And abundant water means abundant water to test them thereby to try them thereby.
72:17: And His statement, And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord - He will drive him into a severe punishment. God Almighty says: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord with which He reminded him, which is this Qur’an, and its meaning is: And whoever turns away from listening to the Qur’an and using it, God will drive him into a severe, arduous punishment. He says: God will drive him into a severe, arduous punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord - He will drive him into a steadily ascending punishment. He said: A hardship of punishment in which he will ascend. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told me, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, an ascending torment, he said: a hardship from the torment. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Isra`il, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Isra`il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A mounting torment. He said: A mountain in Hell. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, He will cause him to go into a steadily ascending punishment is a punishment in which there is no rest. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: An ascending torment. He said: An ascending torment from God in which there is no rest. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, He will cause him to go into a steadily ascending punishment, he said: Ascending is the punishment that is set up. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement He causes him to walk. Some of the reciters of Mecca and Basra read it We cause him to walk with a nun, considering that His statement to test them is with a nun. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with a ya, meaning: God causes him to walk, in response to the Lord in His statement, And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord.
72:18: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say, ‘It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened’ and that the mosques are for God, so do not invoke anyone with God, O people, and do not associate anything with Him in them, but single out His monotheism and devote worship to Him alone. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, “And the mosques are for God, so do not invoke anyone with God,” when the Jews and Christians entered their churches and synagogues, they associated partners with God, so God commanded His Prophet to worship God alone. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Mahmud, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, And that the mosques belong to God, he said: The jinn said to the Prophet of God, How can we come to the mosque when we are far from you, and how can we attend the prayer with you when we are far from you? So the verse was revealed, And that the mosques belong to God, so do not invoke anyone along with God. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the mosques are for God, so do not invoke anyone with God. He said: When the Jews and Christians entered their churches and synagogues, they associated partners with God, so God commanded His Prophet to make the call to Him sincere when he entered the mosque. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah: And the mosques belong to God. He said: All of the mosques.
72:19: And his saying: And that when Abdullah stood up to call upon Him, they almost gathered around him in groups means: And that when Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to call upon God, saying: There is no god but God, they almost gathered around him in groups means: They almost gathered around Muhammad, one on top of the other. The singular form is labdah, and there are two pronunciations for it: the first is the kasrah of the lam, and whoever breaks it, pluralizes it as labd, and the second is the damma of the lam, and whoever joins it, pluralizes it as labd with the damma of the lam, or labad. And whoever joins it, says labdan, like rak’i’ and ruko’an. The reciters of the regions break the lam of labd, except for Ibn Muhaisin, for he joins it with a damma, and they have the same meaning, except that the reading that the reciters of the regions follow is more beloved to me. The Arabs call the many locusts that have mounted each other labdah, and from this is the saying of Abd Manaf ibn Rib’i al-Hudhali: They were hit by six houses and four, as if a tax collector had been imposed on them. The collector: the locust that collects everything it eats. The commentators differed about those meant by his statement, They almost mounted him. Some of them said: What he meant by that was the jinn who almost mounted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they heard the Qur’an. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And when Abdullah stood up to call upon Him, they were about to gather around him in droves, meaning when they heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, reciting the Qur’an, and they came close to him, but he did not know about them until the Messenger came to him and began to recite it, Say, ‘It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened.’ It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, They almost mounted him in droves, that they almost rode him out of eagerness for what they heard from him of the Qur’an. Abu Ja`far said: Whoever said this statement considered his statement, And that when Abdullah stood up, to be among what was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Thus, its meaning is: Say, it was revealed to me that a group of jinn listened, and that when Abdullah stood up, he called upon Him. Others said: Rather, this is from the words of a group of jinn when they returned to their people and told them what they saw of the obedience of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to him and their following him in bowing and prostrating. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Ma'mar told me: Abu Muslim told us, on the authority of Abu 'Awana, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The jinn said to their people, When 'Abdullah stood up to call upon Him, they almost covered him with a crowd. He said: When they saw him praying and his companions bowing as he bowed and prostrating as he prostrated, they were amazed at the obedience of his companions to him. He said: So they said to their people, When 'Abdullah stood up to call upon Him, they almost covered him with a crowd. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ziyad, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: And that when Abdullah stood up to call upon Him, they almost fell upon him in crowds, he said: The companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to follow him, bowing as he bowed, and prostrating as he prostrated. Whoever said this statement that we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Saeed opened the alif in his statement and that he and connected it to his statement, and that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord, with a fatha, and it was permissible for him to close it as an initial letter. Others said: Rather, this is from the report of God that He revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because He knew that mankind and the jinn conspired against him, in order to invalidate the truth that he had brought them, but God refused to do anything but complete it. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And when Abdullah stood up to call upon Him, they were about to gather around him in crowds. He said: The jinn and mankind gathered around this matter to extinguish it, but God refused except to support it, carry it out, and make it prevail over those who opposed it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, to be hidden, he said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up, the jinn and mankind were hidden together, and they were eager to extinguish this light that God had sent down. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, They almost gathered against him in droves, he said: They conspired against him, some against others, they conspired against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And whoever says this statement opens the alif of his statement, and that he. The most correct of the sayings is the one that says: This is report from God that when His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to call to Him, all the Arabs conspired against him and tried to extinguish God’s light. We said that this is the most correct interpretation because his statement, And that when Abdullah stood up to call upon Him, follows his statement, And that the mosques belong to God, and that is from God’s information. Likewise, his statement, And that when Abdullah stood up to call upon Him, and another is that He, the Most High, followed that with his statement, So do not call upon anyone along with God. So it is known that what follows that is the information about what happened to the one commanded not to call upon anyone along with God in that, not the information about the large number of people who answered the call and their haste to answer. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Hudha told us: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And when the servant of God stood up to call upon Him, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up saying, There is no god but God, and called the people to their Lord, the Arabs were almost all against him. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, They almost piled up on him, he said: They piled up on him. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: They almost surrounded him. He said: Some of them surrounded each other. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, They almost became a crowd against him, meaning: helpers. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They almost fell upon him in droves, he said: All of them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: They almost fell upon him in droves. He said: All of them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: They almost covered him with a blanket. A blanket is something that is one part on top of another.
72:20: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, Say, ‘I only call upon my Lord.’ The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufians, read it as a report said with an alif. Whoever reads it like that, makes it a report from God about His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said. So the meaning of the statement is: And when Abdullah stood up to call upon Him, they gathered around him. He said to them, I only call upon my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with Him. Some of the Medinans and the majority of the Kufian reciters read it as a command from God Almighty to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the people who were about to gather around you, I only call upon my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with Him. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.
72:21: And His saying: “Say: I have no power to harm you or to bring you to the right path.” God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of Arabia who rejected the advice you brought them: I have no power to harm you in your religion or in your worldly life, nor to bring you to the right path, because the One who has that power is God, to whom belongs the kingdom of all things.
72:22: And His saying: Say, ‘None of His creation can protect me from God if He wants something from me, nor can anyone help me against Him.’ It was mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because some of the jinn said: I will protect him. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, who said: A Hadrami claimed that it was mentioned to him that a jinn from among their nobles, Dhat Tubba, said: Muhammad only wants us to protect him, and I will protect him. Then God revealed: “Say: No one can protect me from God.” His saying: And I will not find any refuge other than Him, means: I will not find any refuge other than God to which I can resort. As Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, And I will not find any refuge other than Him, meaning: I will not find any refuge other than God to which I can resort. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And I will not find besides Him a refuge: meaning a refuge and a supporter. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Multahidan means: taking refuge. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: And I will not find anyone besides Him to seek refuge. He said: A helper.
72:23: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to the polytheists of Arabia: I do not possess for you any harm or guidance except a message from God and His messages. He says: Except that I convey to you from God what He commanded me to convey to you, and except His messages with which He sent me to you. As for guidance and failure, they are in God’s hand. He owns them, and He alone possesses them. He guides whomever He wills and fails whomever He wills. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, except a message from God and His messages, that is what I possess, a message from God and His messages. This may have another meaning, which is that illa is two letters, and la is separated from in, so the meaning of the statement is: (Say, None will protect me from God if I do not convey His messages. So the accusative of the conveyance is from the implication of a verb of recompense, like the saying of the speaker: In la standing, then sitting, and In la giving, individually, beautifully, meaning: If you do not do the giving individually, beautifully. And His statement: And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger - for him is the fire of Hell. God Almighty says: And whoever disobeys God in what He has commanded and forbidden, and denies Him, and His Messenger, and rejects His messages - for him is the fire of Hell, which he will burn in. They will abide therein forever. He says: They will remain therein forever without end.
72:24: And His statement: Until, when they see what they are promised, God Almighty says: When they see what their Lord promises them of punishment and the establishment of the Hour, they will know who is weaker in support and fewer in number, the soldiers of God whom they associated with Him, or these polytheists with Him.
72:25: God Almighty says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your al-Nas 114:I do not know whether what your Lord promises you of punishment and the Hour is near or whether my Lord will set a term for it. Meaning: a known end whose duration will be long.
72:26: And His statement: He is the Knower of the unseen, and He reveals His secret to no one * Except to a messenger whom He has chosen. What is meant by the Knower of the unseen is that He knows what is hidden from the sight of His creation, so that they have not seen it. He does not reveal His secret to anyone, teaching it or showing it to them, except to a messenger whom He has chosen. Then He reveals it to him in whatever way He wills of that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And He does not disclose His secret to anyone * Except to a messenger with whom He is pleased, so God Almighty informed the messengers of the secret revelation and revealed to them what He revealed to them of His secret, and what God decrees, for no one knows that except Him.
72:27: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, He is the Knower of the unseen, and He reveals His secret to no one * Except to a messenger with whom He is pleased, for He chooses them and informs them of whatever He wills of the unseen. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Except for a Messenger with whom He is pleased, for He reveals it from the unseen as He wills if He is pleased with it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And He does not disclose His secrets to anyone * Except to a messenger with whom He is pleased, he said: He sends down from His secrets whatever He wills to the prophets. He sent down the secret of the unseen to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Qur’an. He said: And He told us in it the secret of what will happen on the Day of Resurrection. His saying: He will send guards and guardians before and behind him, means: He will send guards and guardians before and behind him to protect him. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Marthad, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: Except for a messenger with whom He is pleased, for there will be sent guards before him and behind him. He said: When the angel sent revelation to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would send angels with him to guard him before him and behind him, lest Satan disguise himself in the form of an angel. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim: In front of him and behind him are guards. He said: Angels guarding them from in front of them and from behind them. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: In front of him and behind him are guards. He said: The angels guard him from in front of him and behind him from the jinn. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Talha, meaning Ibn Masraf, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, At his hands and behind him are guards, he said: The angels are guarding him at his hands and behind him, protecting him from the jinn. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Except for a messenger with whom He is pleased, for indeed, there will march before him and behind him guards. He said: They are angels following one another who protect the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Satan until it becomes clear what he was sent with to them, and that is when He says: So that he may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then he will cause to pass before him and behind him an observer, he said: The angels.
72:28: And His statement: So that he may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord. The people of interpretation differed as to what was meant by His statement, So that he may know. Some of them said: What was meant by that was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And they said: The meaning of the statement is: So that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, may know that the messengers before him had conveyed the message of their Lord. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So that he may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord, so that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, may know that the messengers before him had conveyed the message of their Lord and preserved it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: So that he may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord. He said: So that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, may know that the messengers have conveyed the message of God, and that God has preserved them and protected them. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: So that the polytheists may know that the messengers have conveyed the messages of their Lord. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So that he may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord, he said: So that he who denied the messengers may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: So that Muhammad may know that the angels have conveyed the messages of their Lord. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Ya`qub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, “He is the Knower of the unseen, and He reveals His secret to none, * Except to a messenger with whom He is pleased. Then He makes watchers march before him and behind him.” He said: Four guardian angels with Gabriel, so that Muhammad may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord and that He has encompassed what is with them and has taken a number of everything. He said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, did not bring down any revelation except that there were four guardian angels with him. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these sayings in our view is the saying of the one who said: So that the Messenger may know that the Messengers before him had conveyed the messages of their Lord. This is because his saying, So that he may know is the reason for his saying, For He will cause a guard to march before him and behind him, and that is report about the Messenger. Thus it is known that his saying, So that he may know is the reason for it, since that is report about him. His statement: And He encompasses what they have means: He knows everything they have. And He has counted everything means: He knows the number of all things, so nothing of them is hidden from Him. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, that he said regarding this verse, Except for a messenger with whom He is pleased… to His saying, And He has counted all things precisely, he said: So that the messengers may know that their Lord has encompassed them, so that they may convey their messages.
